trust_decision.summary: Each provider's callback middleware decides whether to accept an OAuth authorization code by comparing the request's `state` query with the `state` cookie, and at the pinned commit it accepts the request when both are absent (undefined === undefined); the published fix closes this at seven provider middlewares and leaves the eighth, X (xAuth), fail-open.

landing_point.why: The summary names no provider; Google is the first provider documented in the package README (packages/oauth-providers/README.md:84) and the first test block, so a reader goes to googleAuth.ts and finds the `if (c.req.url.includes('?'))` gate with the `!==` comparison.

fix_sites.entry_point: githubAuth() mounted on GET /github/app and GET /github/oauth-app

O3_reason_to_dismiss: X runs PKCE: with no code-verifier cookie xAuth falls back to a freshly generated verifier (packages/oauth-providers/src/providers/x/xAuth.ts:30), so a forged callback cannot be exchanged and the state check looks redundant; the report and the fix's updated tests name the other providers, not X, and X's own state-less success test still passes (packages/oauth-providers/src/index.test.ts:788-798).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Login initiation must keep redirecting: a request to the same middleware that carries query parameters but no `code` (e.g. the /google-custom-params route with login_hint, prompt, state and access_type, or a configured static `options.state`) must still set the `state` cookie and 302 to the provider; a fix that demands a matching state on every request turns these into 401s, which is why the published fix gates on `auth.code` (googleAuth.ts:20 for `options.state`).

O6_input_shapes: code present, no state query, no state cookie (the original bypass: undefined === undefined)
code present, state query present, state cookie absent
code present, no state query, state cookie present
code present, state query mismatched with the cookie
code present, state query matching the cookie (legitimate path)
no code, other query params present (login initiation must still redirect, not 401)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /x callback through xAuth(): `?code=...` with no `state` query and no `state` cookie is accepted because `c.req.query('state') !== getCookie(c,'state')` is undefined !== undefined; xAuth is public via the ./x subpath (packages/oauth-providers/package.json:33) and its state cookie also lacks the Secure/SameSite attributes the fix adds to the other seven.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: PKCE fallback at xAuth.ts:30 (fresh code_verifier when the cookie is missing) means an attacker's code cannot be exchanged, so a solver can argue the state check is redundant for X; the report's example providers do not include X.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same npm package, one provider directory away; separate package entry point @hono/oauth-providers/x

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a ninth provider directory providers/<name>/<name>Auth.ts carrying the same copied cookie-vs-query gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the package grew provider by provider (x, discord, twitch, msentra are later additions on top of the original four) and every provider copies the same eight-line block, so a new provider is the natural place for another instance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an app-token or hybrid branch that reuses the same `state` cookie for a request that never carries a `code`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: `appAuth` already skips the redirect branch and reaches the state comparison with both values undefined, so extending that mode to a login path is a small plausible change that the same check would have to gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a token-passthrough callback that skips the code exchange when an `access_token` query is supplied
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: googleAuth and msentraAuth already read `access_token`/`expires_in` into the flow's token, and githubAuth.ts:120 and linkedinAuth.ts:101 already skip getTokenFromCode() when a token exists, so gating on `code` alone would not cover a token-only callback.

O9_family: OAuth callback authentication / CSRF state validation (CWE-352 login CSRF, CWE-1275 sensitive cookie without SameSite)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 11.9.0 workspace, Node >=18.4, vitest 4 (vitest.config.ts per package), tsdown build, tsc project references
O10_build.project_tests: packages/oauth-providers/src/index.test.ts (vitest) with msw handlers mocking every provider endpoint in packages/oauth-providers/mocks.ts; run with `pnpm -F @hono/oauth-providers test` or `pnpm vitest run packages/oauth-providers`. The omitted-state 401 path makes no network call.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject only a mismatched state and keep `undefined` passing (e.g. `if (c.req.query('state') && c.req.query('state') !== storedState)`), so the existing no-state success tests such as packages/oauth-providers/src/index.test.ts:547-548 stay green and the hole remains.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/oidc-auth/src/index.ts:430-436 is a second package that also validates OAuth state, but it delegates to oauth4webapi's validateAuthResponse and requires the code_verifier/nonce cookies (index.ts:454), so the omitted-state fail-open does not carry over; not pursued.
packages/mcp/src/auth/helpers/authorize.test.ts:372-394 handles client-side state passthrough for MCP and is unrelated to this protection; not pursued.
